questions.question: A & B together earn ₹840 for a job. A works the whole time; B joins after the job is 25% done. B is twice as efficient as A. Find B's share.
questions.questionHtml: A & B together earn ₹840 for a job. A works the whole time; B joins after the job is 25% done. B is twice as efficient as A. Find B's share.
questions.solution:
Let A's rate = 1 unit/day; then B's rate = 2 units/day.

A works alone for 25% of the work, then both work together for remaining 75%.

Time taken by A alone for 25% = same as time for both to do remaining 75% (since 3 units/day combined vs 1 unit/day alone).

So A and B each contribute 50% of total work.

Hence A's share = B's share = ₹840/2 = ₹420.

questions.question: Given: x + 1/x = −2, then determine the value of x⁶ + 1/x⁶ − 3(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) + 4(x² + 1/x²).
questions.questionHtml: Given: x + 1/x = −2, then determine the value of x⁶ + 1/x⁶ − 3(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) + 4(x² + 1/x²).
questions.solution:
x + 1/x = −2 ⇒ x = −1.

All even powers of −1 equal 1, so x² + 1/x² = 2, x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 2, x⁶ + 1/x⁶ = 2.

Expression = 2 − 3(2) + 4(2) = 2 − 6 + 8 = 4.

questions.question: A sum becomes 2.5 times of itself in 5 years under simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: A sum becomes 2.5 times of itself in 5 years under simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
For 2.5 times: principal becomes 2.5P, so SI = 1.5P.

1.5P = P × R × 5/100 ⇒ R = 30%.

For 5 times: SI = 4P. 4P = P × 30 × T/100 ⇒ T = 400/30 = 40/3 = 13⅓ years.

questions.question: A tank is in the shape of a rectangular parallelepiped of size 50 m × 40 m × 3 m. Its capacity in kilolitres is:
questions.questionHtml: A tank is in the shape of a rectangular parallelepiped of size 50 m × 40 m × 3 m. Its capacity in kilolitres is:
questions.solution:
Volume = 50 × 40 × 3 = 6000 m³.

1 m³ = 1000 litres = 1 kilolitre.

Hence capacity = 6,000 kilolitres.

questions.question: A right circular cone having height of 30 cm is cut by two parallel planes at heights 10 cm and 20 cm from the base. What is the ratio of the volumes of the three parts (from top to bottom)?
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cone having height of 30 cm is cut by two parallel planes at heights 10 cm and 20 cm from the base. What is the ratio of the volumes of the three parts (from top to bottom)?
questions.solution:
From apex, cuts are at heights 10 and 20 (measured from apex).

Volume of cone of height h from apex ∝ h³.

Top cone (h = 10): proportional to 1000.

Middle frustum (h = 20 part − h = 10 part): proportional to 8000 − 1000 = 7000.

Bottom frustum (h = 30 − h = 20): proportional to 27000 − 8000 = 19000.

Ratio = 1000 : 7000 : 19000 = 1 : 7 : 19.

questions.question: A solid hemisphere of radius R is melted and recast into n smaller hemispheres of radius r. Find the value of n.
questions.questionHtml: A solid hemisphere of radius R is melted and recast into n smaller hemispheres of radius r. Find the value of n.
questions.solution:
Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr_radius³.

By conservation of volume: (2/3)πR³ = n × (2/3)πr³.

n = R³/r³ = (R/r)³.

questions.question: A sector has a central angle of 90° and a radius of 6 cm. Another sector has a central angle of π/2 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.questionHtml: A sector has a central angle of 90° and a radius of 6 cm. Another sector has a central angle of π/2 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.solution:
π/2 radians = 90°.

Both sectors share the same central angle (90°) and the same radius.

Hence their areas are equal — ratio = 1 : 1.

questions.question: A regular polygon has each interior angle measuring 150°. Find the number of its sides.
questions.questionHtml: A regular polygon has each interior angle measuring 150°. Find the number of its sides.
questions.solution:
Each interior angle = (n − 2) × 180°/n = 150°.

180n − 360 = 150n ⇒ 30n = 360 ⇒ n = 12.

Hence the polygon has 12 sides.

questions.question: A point P is 13 cm away from the center of a circle. A tangent is drawn from P to the circle, and its length is 12 cm. What is the area of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: A point P is 13 cm away from the center of a circle. A tangent is drawn from P to the circle, and its length is 12 cm. What is the area of the circle?
questions.solution:
For tangent from external point: r² + 12² = 13².

r² = 169 − 144 = 25 ⇒ r = 5.

Area = π r² = 25π cm².

questions.question: In △ABC, an angle bisector from A meets BC at D. If AD bisects ∠BAC, and AB = AC, are △ABD and △ACD congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.questionHtml: In △ABC, an angle bisector from A meets BC at D. If AD bisects ∠BAC, and AB = AC, are △ABD and △ACD congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.solution:
In △ABD and △ACD: AB = AC (given), ∠BAD = ∠CAD (since AD bisects ∠BAC), AD = AD (common).

Two sides and the included angle equal — SAS congruence.

Hence they are congruent by SAS.

questions.question: If sinA = x, then what is cos²A in terms of x?
questions.questionHtml: If sinA = x, then what is cos²A in terms of x?
questions.solution:
By the Pythagorean identity, sin²A + cos²A = 1.

cos²A = 1 − sin²A = 1 − x².

questions.question: The angle between two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 60°. What is the angle subtended by the chord connecting their points of contact at the center?
questions.questionHtml: The angle between two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 60°. What is the angle subtended by the chord connecting their points of contact at the center?
questions.solution:
For tangents from an external point with included angle θ, the angle subtended at the centre between the radii to the points of contact is 180° − θ.

180° − 60° = 120°.

Hence the central angle = 120°.

questions.question: From a point P outside a circle, a tangent PA and a secant PBC are drawn. If PA = 6 cm and BC = 5 cm, what is the length of the segment PB?
questions.questionHtml: From a point P outside a circle, a tangent PA and a secant PBC are drawn. If PA = 6 cm and BC = 5 cm, what is the length of the segment PB?
questions.solution:
By tangent-secant relation from external point: PA² = PB × PC.

6² = PB × (PB + 5).

PB² + 5 PB − 36 = 0.

(PB + 9)(PB − 4) = 0 ⇒ PB = 4 cm.
